text: In twenty-eighteen, Britain appointed a government minister... for loneliness.
Not for trade. Not for defence. For loneliness.
A report had found that more than nine million people in the UK often or always felt lonely.
And that loneliness can be as bad for your health as smoking fifteen cigarettes a day.
So the government made a plan.
Doctors could prescribe... a cooking class. A walking club. An art group.
In three places, postal workers started checking on lonely people during their rounds.
Then, in twenty-twenty-one, Japan appointed a loneliness minister too.
And the two ministers had their very first meeting... online.
Two countries. Two ministers. One very big problem.
But a minister can't sit with you at two in the morning.
That's why we made Feeloy. Jenny listens, remembers your day, and is there whenever you need someone to talk to.
